title: Mixed-surface Gravel G1 pre-ride check
summary: Check tires, wheels, brakes, drivetrain and mounted equipment before a ride that may move between pavement and rough surfaces.

steps.title: Inspect both tires and verify pressure
steps.instruction: Check for cuts, casing damage, embedded debris, poor bead seating or visible sealant leakage where applicable. Measure pressure against the actual tire/rim/load guidance for the planned surface.
steps.why: Tire condition and pressure strongly affect support, traction and rim protection on rough surfaces.
steps.warning: Do not ride a tire with structural casing damage, an unexplained bulge or unsafe bead seating.
steps.check: Both tires appear structurally sound and pressure is within the real system limits.

steps.title: Check wheels and braking
steps.instruction: Spin both wheels, look for obvious wobble or rubbing, and operate both brakes during a stationary then controlled low-speed check.
steps.why: Mixed-surface impacts can affect wheel alignment and braking components.
steps.warning: Stop if braking is weak, inconsistent, leaking or if a wheel/rotor shows unsafe interference.
steps.check: Wheels rotate acceptably and both brakes respond predictably.

steps.title: Inspect the exposed 1× drivetrain
steps.instruction: Check chain, chainring, cassette and rear derailleur for obvious damage, severe contamination, poor alignment or abnormal movement.
steps.why: Gravel drivetrains are exposed to dust, water and impact that can affect shifting and wear.
steps.warning: Do not put fingers or cloth into the moving drivetrain while rotating the cranks or wheel.
steps.check: No obvious drivetrain damage or unsafe interference is visible.

steps.title: Check cockpit and anything mounted to the bike
steps.instruction: Inspect the handlebar/controls and any accessories or luggage attached to frame/fork mounts. Nothing should be loose or able to enter a wheel, brake, drivetrain or steering path.
steps.why: Rough surfaces can loosen hardware and make poor cargo retention more consequential.
steps.warning: Use actual component torque and mounting specifications rather than guessing.
steps.check: Controls and mounted equipment appear secure and clear of moving parts.
